# **Exterior of the Volume**

The book is bound in a style typical of its period, featuring a sturdy spine and decorative covers. The spine is bound in a light-colored, cream-colored material—likely <term>vellum<note>A high-quality parchment made from calfskin, frequently used for durable book bindings.</note></term> or tawed leather—which shows horizontal ridges indicating the internal cords used to sew the pages together.

The front cover is finished with **marbled paper**, displaying an intricate pattern of interlocking, organic swirls in shades of dark blue, gray, reddish-brown, and pale yellow.

## Preface.

->Reader, beloved in God of eternal love!<-

Because I believe that the summary description of these letters on the preceding title page will likely make you eager <note>The original German "lüstern" suggests a strong, almost physical longing or appetite, here applied to a spiritual hunger for the text.</note> to read them and to see the matters described therein the moment you see it, I do not wish to delay you with a long preface. Instead, I will say only a few words to mention certain necessary things for your benefit and instruction.

And indeed, I first report to you—and can assure you in truth—that in the publication of these letters, I seek nothing other than the glory of my God and the benefit of my dear neighbor. I ask you, therefore, that you make this sole objective <term>Augenmerck<gloss>literally "eye-mark"; the specific target or focus one keeps in view</gloss></term> of mine your own as well. Read them with pure intentions in the fear of the Lord, and apply everything to the glorification of God’s great name and to the salvation of your soul <note>original: "Seelen Heil," referring to the spiritual well-being and eternal safety of the soul</note>.

Yes, I ask you to read them in the fear of the Lord with an impartial mind, to test everything well and keep that which is good, and to apply it to God’s glory and your eternal welfare; should you

### The First Letter.

->My yet unknown, but in the Lord Jesus most heartily beloved heart and friend!<-

It is certainly a great joy for a Christian <term>pilgrim<gloss>A central metaphor in 18th-century Pietism, viewing the believer as a traveler passing through the world's hardships toward a heavenly home</gloss></term> or a true child of God, when on their pilgrimage they find someone who understands their language and asks after God, and is thus of one mind and will to travel through the great and cruel wildernesses of this world toward the heavenly <term>Canaan<gloss>In the Bible, the Promised Land; in this context, it represents heaven or the final state of spiritual rest</gloss></term>.

And because I have now heard from the bearer of this letter that <term>Your Dear Self<gloss>original: "E. L." (Eure Liebden); a respectful and affectionate form of address used among the nobility or within spiritual communities, roughly meaning "Your Charity" or "Your Belovedness"</gloss></term> is such a person who fears and seeks God, and takes the salvation of their soul to heart; then I rightly rejoice in the Lord, and my soul is glad in my God—both over my good fortune in having found and met such a good friend and traveling companion on my troubled <note>original: "Wohlfarth"; while it usually means "welfare," here it refers to the "faring" or journeying of the soul through life's trials</note> journey, as well as over your own great

## The Second Letter.

->which contains an answer to the preceding letter along with several questions.<-

### My beloved and very worthy friend!

Your correspondence—previously unknown to me, but now just made known—is all the more pleasing to me, as I have seen from the letter itself as well as from the shared enclosures, if (as I do not doubt) you are the sole author thereof, what a great measure of grace and <term>illumination<gloss>original: "Erleichtungs-Maaß"; refers to the spiritual "light" or insight granted by God to understand divine truths</gloss></term> God has bestowed upon you; regarding which you, just like **St. Paul**, will not exalt yourself in your glory in God, but will instead attribute everything to and give thanks for the overflowing Divine grace.

One finds in you a truly living example of how God chooses what the world calls and deems lowly, and in contrast puts the high to shame <note>A reference to 1 Corinthians 1:27: "But God hath chosen the foolish things of the world to confound the wise..." This reflects the Pietist value of "heart-religion" over formal academic theology.</note>; from which one can clearly grasp that for the building up of true wisdom and understanding in Divine things, no natural skill or scholarship, but rather only a humble bowing before God and the subsequent Divine illumination brings and assists [one].

I have read through your explanation of the <term>Restoration of All Things<gloss>original: "Wiederbringung aller Dinge"; the theological doctrine that all people and fallen angels will eventually be saved and reconciled with God</gloss></term> and found it all to be good; just as I have also been corresponding for some time with the dear and enlightened Mr. Schäfer <note>Johann David Schäfer (1657–1725), a radical Pietist leader often persecuted for his universalist views.</note> regarding this as well as many other matters, and give my full approval to the cause; this, however, I cannot yet comprehend, that one, with such

<meta>The page ends with the catchword "Leh," suggesting the next page continues with the word "Lehre" (teaching) or "Lehrart" (manner of teaching).</meta>

He also confirms his agreement with the controversial doctrine of Universal Restoration and his ongoing correspondence with the Pietist Johann David Schäfer.</summary>
<keywords>illumination, St. Paul, humility, Restoration of All Things, Johann David Schäfer, scholarship, grace</keywords>

--- Page 18 ---
<meta>This page continues the "Second Letter" begun on page 12. The text continues a discussion regarding a specific individual (likely the correspondent or an associate named Lehr) who is considering a total separation from the established church—a common theme among Radical Pietists of the era.</meta>

Lehre <note>Likely the conclusion of a surname, possibly Johann Daniel Lehr, mentioned on the previous page.</note> himself wants to completely separate from our church, even though the abuse in such [a church]—as well as that of the **Holy Supper** <note>Also known as Holy Communion or the Eucharist.</note>—is great; one cannot, however, dispense with the church in the instruction of children and other simple folk, nor in the public **Act of Baptism**, where everyone who is asked to be a **baptismal witness** <note>original: "Tauff-Zeuge"; a godparent or official witness to the rite.</note> must indeed appear. And because I then hear that he is also entirely absenting himself from the churches, I would like to know the reason for this briefly and in writing; this, as well as the sharing of the printed document, would be doing me a favor.

Mr. Schäfer also posits the <term>Millennium<gloss>original: "tausend jährige Reich"; the prophesied thousand-year reign of Christ on earth mentioned in Revelation 20</gloss></term>; a double resurrection; the conversion of the Jews during those thousand years; the movement of the heavens and the earth before the thousand years, but their transformation after the same; the granting of grace to the so-called <term>Half-Christians<gloss>original: "Halb-Christen"; a term used for those who were outwardly religious but lacked what Pietists considered a "living faith" or true rebirth</gloss></term> lying imprisoned in the first death, after the thousand-year kingdom, in the final resurrection, according to **Revelation 20:14–15** <note>original: "Apoc. 20/ 14. 15."</note>; the breaking of the first seal which has now begun, according to **Revelation 6** <note>original: "Apoc. 6"</note>; and the impending, terrifying judgments, and the condemnation of the **Babylonian Whore** and the **Antichrist** <note>In this period, Radical Pietists often identified "Babylon" and the "Whore" with the corrupt state church systems (both Catholic and Protestant) that they believed were persecuting true believers.</note> following soon thereafter. ### The Third Letter.

#### Honored Sir and Friend!

I have received your letter <note>The author uses the formal third-person "He" (*Er*) common in 18th-century German polite address, here translated as "you."</note>, and regarding what you first mentioned therein concerning me and my previous letter, together with the little pamphlet I sent—namely, that you perceived from it that God has bestowed upon me a great measure of **grace** and **enlightenment**, provided that I am indeed the sole **author** of it—to this I reply that it is indeed so: I am the sole author of that little work. Furthermore, it did not cost me much "racking of brains" <note>original: "Kopf-verbrechens"; literally "head-breaking," meaning intense mental exertion.</note>, for it was almost finished in a few hours or within a single day. You may well believe me in this; for because I know that God the Lord is an enemy to all liars from the bottom of His heart, and that in the mouths of the **144,000 Virgins of the Lamb** <note>A reference to Revelation 14:1–5, describing the redeemed "firstfruits" who follow Christ and in whose mouth "was found no guile."</note> no deceit may be found, I have for many years now applied myself to the **Truth**. Thus, you may certainly believe my words. Indeed, according to the fundamental rule of this precious **Truth**, which is so very dear to me, I neither can nor may deny that the dear God has measured out to me a considerable portion of His grace, and has given a bright ray and reflection of His eternal **Light** into my otherwise so poor and darkened heart and soul. In this light, I now also see the true light and know how to distinguish it to a fair degree from the **darkness**. # The Fifth Letter.

### Jesus our Light and Life!

->My beloved and highly esteemed friend in Him!<-

I have duly received your dear letter and answer it here very briefly. First, regarding your hesitation, where you mention finding it somewhat questionable that the **children of God** are all ruled by one Spirit—who is in Himself only of one kind—and yet here and there they do not agree with one another but still hold different opinions on various matters. In this regard, you specifically highlight the **Coming of Christ** <term>Zukunfft Christi; the Second Coming or Advent</term>, which Mr. Sch. <note>likely a reference to a contemporary Pietist or theologian</note> considers to be further off than I do. To this I offer the friendly answer: it is indeed an eternal truth that the children and instruments of God are all ruled and driven by one and the same **Holy Spirit** of God. And that the **Holy Spirit** is in Himself unified or of one kind, and thus can never contradict Himself.

However, that the **children of God** <term>Kinder GOttes; a term for those who have experienced a spiritual rebirth</term> nevertheless hold different opinions on many things—and specifically that one considers the heartfelt **Coming of Christ** to be nearer than another—stems in part from the fact that such **mysteries** <term>Geheimnüsse; divine truths revealed by the Spirit rather than human reason</term> are recognized and perceived by them only with the inward eyes of the spirit and of faith, in the **Mirror of Wisdom** <term>Spiegel der Weißheit; a concept common in German mysticism (like that of Jacob Böhme), where Divine Wisdom reflects the eternal reality and thoughts of God</term> and of eternity. In this mirror, what is near and far are all one thing, and a thousand years are to be counted as only one day. Thus, in this matter and because of this cause, no one can know the actual time and hour, which God...

After I had already closed this, I found in my room a small slip of paper in his hand <note>The author likely refers to a student or correspondent whose questions he is about to answer.</note>, upon which the following two questions were written: 1) Were the angels also created during the six days at the beginning of the creation of this world? 2) Does Moses in Genesis 3:1 mean the natural serpent?

He continues until his appearance at the Last Judgment to triumph and rule over death, the devil, sin, and the children of darkness. This follows after—as seen in Chapter 5:9–10—the **Eternal Gospel** or the **Restoration of All Things** <note>original: "Wiederbringung aller Dinge"; the controversial doctrine of "Universalism," which suggests that all people, and perhaps even fallen angels, will eventually be saved and returned to God</note> is sung, first by the **Church Triumphant** <note>The believers and angels already in heaven</note> above in heaven, and afterward by the **Church Militant** <note>The body of believers currently struggling against sin on earth</note> here on earth during the first seal. It continues until it is finally sung as a **new song** upon the earth by the **144,000** (Chapter 14:2–3) collectively, and proclaimed most powerfully and without hindrance to the whole world by the **two witnesses** <note>Two prophetic figures mentioned in Revelation 11 who preach before the end of the age</note> (Chapter 11). One should not look for them among the children of darkness or the godless children of the world, who indeed never had the slightest Divine warmth of the new spirit and life of love within them, and thus could also not have lost it therein; which my beloved friend should consider further. 

And if he should perhaps ask me further: which **Church Period** <note>original: *Kirchen-Periodus*; a theological framework where the seven churches of Revelation represent seven successive eras of Christian history.</note> then might now (in my thoughts) have the upper hand in this time of ours? And what is worst: all these lukewarm and wretched Laodiceans still firmly imagine that they are very rich, and have had their fill, and need nothing more for their adornment. ### The Ninth Letter.

### Which is a response to the previous questions.

->Beloved Sir and Christian Friend!<-

I have duly received your letter and noted its contents; I find myself also inclined and bound to provide an answer to all your inquiries, according to the measure and light of grace and knowledge which God shall impart to me for this purpose.

It is indeed true that I have never previously concerned myself with the specific knowledge and science of the secret things <note>The author is likely referring to "secret things" or *mysteria*—esoteric or deeply prophetic interpretations of the Bible common in 17th and 18th-century mystical theology.</note> about which you ask me here; as I already mentioned in my previous message, I consequently have but little knowledge of them. ### Response.

Yes, such souls are certainly to be interpreted as all true martyrs from the time of Christ until then; however, one must note this: not all who appear to have been slain for the sake of the **Word of God** <note>original: "Wort GOTTes"</note> are to be counted among them without distinction. For indeed, in the old and new **heretic and sect wars**, or **religious wars**, <note>A reference to the violent denominational conflicts following the Reformation, such as the Thirty Years' War, which the author views as political rather than truly spiritual.</note> many millions have perished who were then presented or held by their allies to be holy and steadfast martyrs. ### The Twenty-Fifth Question.

Whether the **Leviathan** and **Behemoth** in Job <note>original: "Hiob."</note> are only one or two distinct creatures. Likewise, whether the serpent in Paradise or the dragon in the Apocalypse <note>The Book of Revelation.</note> represent more than just Lucifer and his angels as the **Leviathan** in Job.

->Answer.<-

That the **Leviathan** indicates the spirit of the great internal **fire-world**, and the **Behemoth** indicates the spirit of this external world—and thus they represent two different creatures—I have already mentioned in the previous question. However, the serpent in Paradise and the dragon in the Apocalypse are to be understood as being of the **Leviathan** or the great **fire-spirit** of the dark abyss, and by no means as Lucifer and his angels, to be [under]- <note>The text ends mid-word. The catchword "ste" suggests the word "verstehen," meaning "to understand" or "to be understood."</note>

### The Eleventh Letter.
->Honored Mr. District Official.<-

Regarding your objection to my previous thoughts concerning the **hour of temptation**, it is certainly as you report, that the testing of the believers under the Antichrist’s rage and persecution can also be called an "hour of temptation," since the believers are indeed tempted or tested therein to the highest degree. I did not deny this in my previous letter; I only say that this is not *the* **Hour of Temptation** which is to come upon all the inhabitants of the earth <note>A reference to Revelation 3:10, which describes a specific period of global trial from which the faithful are sometimes said to be "kept."</note>. And even the children of God are not preserved from this [persecution], since they must go right into the midst of it, and for the most part must give up their lives within it. For this [persecution] comes only upon the few children of God, and they are tested therein as to how faithful they wish to remain to the Lord. But when these have first drunk their allotted portion <note>original: "bescheidenen Theil," meaning the specific share assigned or "decided" for them.</note> from the cup of the Lord, from the bitter water, then it shall soon thereafter be offered to all the inhabitants of the earth. <meta>This page continues the theological discourse from the previous page, specifically debating the interpretation of the "new song" mentioned in the Book of Revelation. The author argues against the idea that current radical teachings are entirely "new," instead framing them as a revival of the original Gospel message promised to Adam.</meta>

<page-num>370</page-num>

...one seeks to maintain <note>meaning to argue or defend a position</note> that the new songs of the Elders and the Lamb-Virgins in Revelation 5 and 14 <note>original: "Apoc. 5. und 14."</note> are prophecies concerning this proclamation; yet I cannot find the slightest trace within them of how one can rightly call this teaching a "new song." Unless, perhaps, one understands it in the same way that John writes of the Law of Love: that it was indeed the Old Law which they had heard from the beginning, and which—after a fairly long pause or silence—was sung once again anew or afresh because the great darkness has passed, and the true light now shines brightly once more in various pious hearts.

For on what ground would one want to call this teaching a "new song," since it is indeed the very oldest that has ever been sung in the world? Just as God the Lord himself sang it immediately upon the Fall of Adam, when he spoke: **"The seed of the woman shall crush the serpent's head"**; and just as God the Lord himself thus sang it first, right at the Fall of Man, so all his holy prophets have indeed sung it after Him throughout the course of the world, as Peter himself testifies in Acts 3:21 <note>original: "Actor. 3 / 21."</note>. And after this, Christ himself sang it, and all his holy apostles sang it after him with joy, as can be seen in all their letters; and especially in Paul's letters, who expressed it as clearly as the sun shines at bright midday. ## The Sixteenth Letter.

->Most Valued Friend!<-

In citing the passage of 1 Timothy 4:3 in my previous letter, it was not at all my intention to place Your Kindness <note>original: "Ew. L." (Eure Liebe), a respectful form of address common in Pietist correspondence, literally "Your Love."</note> into such a heretical guild. Rather, I only wished for that passage to be well considered, to see if it might not resemble a secret prohibition—to say that no married pious people could reach the distinguished number of the Bride of Christ <note>In mystical tradition, the "Bride of Christ" refers to the community of believers or specific souls who have reached a state of spiritual union with the Divine.</note>. This was truly my meaning and intent; especially since Paul, in 1 Timothy 3:2, expressly writes that a bishop—who must certainly apply himself to the highest holiness—should be the husband of one wife. For the rest, the single state <term>single state</term> <note>original: "ledigen Stand." Referring to celibacy or remaining unmarried.</note> certainly retains its praise according to the admonitions of Christ and Paul. Yet I do not see what special holiness one should seek therein, even according to the opinion of those who believe that in the beginning of creation, the man Adam was not created for that purpose <note>A reference to theosophical views (like those of Jacob Böhme) suggesting that Adam was originally a self-procreating, androgynous being before the "fall" into gendered division.</note>. Thus, I understand the "not being defiled with women" in Revelation 14 <note>original: "Apoc. 14."</note> according to the explanations in Proverbs 9:13 and Luke 14:26–27. However, I maintain that those who understand our current final times and the proximity of the Day of Christ, and who are still in the single state, will not seek much to exchange it for the married state.

The matter of the internal fire-spirit <term>fire-spirit</term> <note>original: "Feuer-Geist." As noted on the previous page, this refers to the raw, potentially wrathful energy of the soul that requires divine light to be transformed.</note> I find, the longer I consider it, the less to be without foundation. I only ask whether such a thing is the Leviathan in Job, just as Behemoth must signify the outer world-spirit <term>world-spirit</term> <note>original: "Welt-Geist." The governing spiritual atmosphere or "breath" of the physical, temporal world.</note>? And whether this latter one is also constant, and

Without doubt, a noble, fallen prince-angel and an extremely evil and seductive spirit inhabited such an idol, and now and then—by God’s permission—actually performed certain deceptive miracles <note>original: "Miracul"</note>, thereby strengthening the poor blind people, who after all desired to be deceived, in their error.

And these, briefly, are my thoughts on Beelzebub. I have previously mentioned that the founders of such an idol had their eyes upon the Behemoth or the <term>Archeos</term> <note>In the chemical and mystical philosophy of the 17th century, the "Archeus" was considered the vitalizing force of nature or the "internal master" of a substance; here, the author views it as a corrupted natural power.</note> and, for the reason mentioned, brought him sacrifices and worship. 2.) Secondly, he asks why the **fallen angels** cannot attain **repentance and grace** with God before the **Day of Judgment** just as well as fallen humans?

# The eighth letter. U. May 22, 1727.

->The Lord Jesus be our light and life, and our heart’s only joy and delight in time and eternity!<-

->My dear and esteemed Sir and Christian friend!<-

Although I find myself at present somewhat weary and unskillful for writing, I nonetheless consider myself bound to you, and am also willing and inclined to answer your new inquiries according to the measure of grace and the light of <term>knowledge<note>original: "Erkäntnüs," implying an experiential or spiritual understanding rather than mere intellectual facts.</note></term> that the Lord will grant me for it.

And as for your first question concerning <term>J. B.<note>Jacob Boehme (1575–1624), a German Lutheran layman and mystic whose complex cosmological writings were highly influential among 18th-century spiritualists.</note></term>, know, my beloved friend, that such a dear and blessed man built his entire structure or work in all his writings on the foundation of the seven <term>source-spirits<note>original: "Quell-Geister." In Boehme’s system, these are the seven fundamental qualities or forces that constitute both the divine nature and the created world.</note></term>, or forms of nature, and the <term>three principles<note>original: "drey Principien." Boehme's framework describing the "dark world" of God's fire, the "light world" of God's love, and the "outer world" of the physical universe.</note></term>. Whoever does not well perceive and understand such a deep foundation in the light of God cannot understand his language at all, let him be otherwise as learned and of as sharp an intellect as he will. And I certainly hold that such knowledge and understanding can come to no one else, or through any other means, than through <term>rebirth<note>original: "Wiedergeburt." A central concept in Pietism and mysticism, referring to a radical inner transformation by the Holy Spirit.</note></term>, and that this—namely, the new birth—is the only master key to his deep writings. Whoever lacks this must certainly remain outside his pleasure-garden and cannot [see] the beautiful little flowers—I mean the mysteries and

### 5th Form: Light/Love.

The holy, spiritual desire of love—where the holy will of God has sharpened itself in the strict impression and revealed itself through the fire with the power of Almightiness—now leads itself out through the fire into the light. It has thus introduced itself into the powers, into life and movement, and into <term>desire<note>original: "Begierde." For Boehme, desire is the fundamental creative hunger or "urge" that drives all of existence to manifest.</note></term>, wherein the holy birth and the Kingdom of Joy of God’s great love exists and is revealed.

### 6th Form: Sound/Resonance/Word.

This is the sound of the Divine Word arising from the divine powers, which forms itself in the desire of love and leads into an audible Word of all powers. Within this, the revelation of the Divine Kingdom of Joy stands in the free delight of God's wisdom.

### 7th Form: Being/Housing.

This is the formed <term>being<note>original: "Wesen." Often translated as "substance" or "essence," referring to the actualized reality of spiritual forces.</note></term> of the powers, serving as a revelation of those powers. Whatever the first six forms are in spirit, the seventh is in the tangible; it is a <term>housing<note>original: "Gehäusse." This refers to the external shell, body, or container that holds the spiritual forces, representing the manifestation of the spiritual into the physical realm.</note></term> for all the others, or a body of the spirit, within which the spirit works and plays with itself. It is also a food for the fire, from which the fire draws its essence for its consumption, wherein it burns. This seventh form is the Kingdom of God’s Glory; and the seven are named thus:

Revelation chapter 12. And how is the Dragon's casting out from heaven onto the earth to be understood? Also, whether such casting out is to be understood as being of the great <term>wrath-fire-spirit</term> <note>original: *Zorn-Feuer-Geist*; in theosophical writing of this period, this refers to the dark, consuming aspect of nature or the "wrath" of God's fire principle.</note> or <term>Leviathan</term> <note>A biblical sea monster, here used as a mystical symbol for the foundational spirit of malice or the dark principle of the world.</note> himself, or rather of the fallen angels? ->Answer.<-

If one wishes to rightly understand this battling of Michael with the Dragon, and the Dragon's expulsion, it is necessary to investigate the cause of why such a battle begins and occurs; and when we do this, we find that this battle concerns a pregnant woman who is about to give birth; of which John then writes thus in Chapter 12, verse 1: "And there appeared a great sign in heaven: A woman clothed with the sun, and the moon under her feet, and upon her head a crown of twelve stars."

This verse I understand thus: The heaven in which this great sign occurs, of which John writes here, signifies the inner regions or realms of this world which the dragon occupied at the Fall of Adam, and has possessed until now with his forces and powers of wickedness as a mighty prince; he constantly battles the faithful and newborn children of **GOD**, who, according to their <term>inward man</term> <note>A Pauline concept (Romans 7:22) referring to the spiritual part of a person that is regenerated by God, as opposed to the outward, physical body.</note>, still dwell and walk in this heaven during their bodily life (Philippians 3:20), both with his own power of malice as well as with the evil spirits of the fallen angels (and likely the spirits of evil men) and their princes and potentates; regarding which one may consult Ephesians 2:2 and Chapter 6:10–18.

## The 4th Question.

Christ says in **John 18:36**, "My kingdom is not of this world," and yet during the time of the thousand years it shall be on earth, according to the lower church <note>original: *unteren Kirche*; this likely refers to the "Church Militant" or the earthly manifestation of the faithful, in contrast to the "Church Triumphant" in heaven.</note>; how then is this to be understood?

### Answer.

By "this world," of which our beloved Savior says his kingdom is not of it, he understands this present evil world <note>original: *arge Welt*; a common Pietist and mystical term for the current age of sin and spiritual darkness.</note>, in which the devil is still prince and has his kingdom; which world then extends until the second coming of **Christ.**

But at that same time, the almighty **GOD** will first take up the kingdom, and the kingdoms of this world will become the kingdoms of our **GOD** and his **Christ**, and he will reign from eternity to eternity, **Revelation 11:15, Chapter 19:6.** And thus the future thousand-year kingdom of **JESUS Christ**, in which he indeed shall have his kingdom in the world and on earth, and shall rule from one sea to the other <note>A reference to Psalm 72:8, often used to describe the universal reach of the Messiah’s reign.</note>, is not to be counted as part of this present evil world, which will end at the second coming of **Christ**; rather, it is another world, which **Christ** the **Lord** himself in several places calls "that world" <note>original: *jene Welt*; used here to distinguish the Millennial reign or the age to come from the current fallen era.</note>, as in **Matthew 12:32** and **Luke 20:35.**

## The 20th Question.

Whether the opinion of some so-called **Pietists** <term>A movement within Lutheranism that emphasized individual piety, "living faith," and the inner spiritual life over formal dogma.</term> has a basis / that even the **heathens** <term>original: "Heyden," referring here to those who have not heard the Christian Gospel.</term> / who live piously / can be saved without the knowledge of Christ / and that Christ's Spirit can have its work in them without external knowledge?

### Answer.

Without Christ and his living **knowledge** <term>original: "Erkändtnüs." ## The 21st Question.

What does the word *Tophet* in Jeremiah 19 actually signify?

### Answer.

*Tophet* was a certain site or place / in the *Valley of Ben-Hinnom* / which was situated before Jerusalem / near the *Sun Gate* or *Brick Gate* / where they built altars and groves to *Moloch* and *Baal* / and other idols / and sacrificed their sons and daughters or children to such idols / through fire amidst great drumming / kettledrums and the sound of other instruments / and a great noise / so that their screaming <note>original: "kreuschen," an archaic form of "kreischen."</note> might not be heard / as was the custom among the abominable heathen nations / and as is also clear from this 19th and the 7th chapter of this prophet.

### The 22nd Question.

Whether in Isaiah 66:17 something else is to be understood by "swine’s flesh," or if it refers to natural meat?

->Answer.<-

In the Old Covenant, the LORD God had indeed forbidden the Jewish people from eating swine, among other animals. As is well known, they were required to avoid them as unclean—and continue to do so to this day—along with all other animals described to them as such. Whenever they failed to do this, they transgressed God’s commandment and became defiled by those animals. However, God’s primary intention in prohibiting the eating of such animals recognized as "unclean" was not focused so much on the consumption of the meat itself, but rather on the unclean vices in human beings who shared characteristics with those animals. This is similar to how, in the time of Noah, He permitted all flesh to be eaten by mankind just like green herbs <note>A reference to Genesis 9:3, where God tells Noah that every moving thing that lives shall be food.</note>. Thus, by forbidding the eating of such unclean animals, the LORD God primarily intended to forbid His people from those animalistic vices.

For example, a pig is a truly filthy creature. It not only eats all manner of carrion, foul vermin, and stinking dung—saving your presence <note>original: "mit l. v.," likely an abbreviation for *cum licentia venia* or *mit Lust und Vergnügen*, an archaic polite disclaimer used when mentioning something offensive or "gross."</note>—and does so with the greatest greed and envy, but it also finds its greatest pleasure when it can wallow deep in the muck. Because God has forbidden His people from eating swine's flesh, He primarily intended to signal and forbid them from all such swinish filthiness, so that they might not wallow in the mire of sin, nor be as greedy, filthy, and ungrateful in their eating habits as the swine.

<summary>This page provides an allegorical interpretation of the biblical prohibition against eating pork, specifically referencing Isaiah 66:17. The author argues that the law was intended to discourage human vices that mirror the "filthy" nature of pigs rather than just being a literal dietary restriction.</summary>
<keywords>Old Testament, Isaiah 66:17, dietary laws, purity, swine's flesh, allegory, vices, Jewish people, Noah, symbolism</keywords>

### The 25th Question.
Whether Isaiah 30:26 refers to the 1,000 years or the renewed world?

->Answer.<-

I understand this passage to refer to the 1,000-year glorious kingdom <note>This refers to the "Millennium," a period of peace and holiness on earth described in Revelation 20.</note> of Jesus Christ. At that time, not only will nature experience a noticeable increase and elevation in its powers—after being somewhat cleansed of its curse through the vengeance and great fiery zeal of the Lord, and after the land has been purified of its idols and evil inhabitants—so that the natural sun, moon, and stars will shine brighter and the earth will yield more abundant and better fruits; but especially Christ, the Sun of Righteousness <note>original: *Sonne der Gerechtigkeit*, a reference to Malachi 4:2, often applied to Christ's second coming.</note>, will shine seven times brighter in His church-heaven <note>The author uses "church-heaven" to describe the spiritual atmosphere or state of the believers' community.</note> at that time than He does at this present time. Furthermore, the radiance and light of the lower churches on earth—which until then are compared to the changeable light of the moon, which now wanes and now waxes, being sometimes light and then again dark and empty—will at that same time be like the sunshine. That is to say, it will no longer be subject to any change, just as it is written: that at that time their sun should no longer go down, because the Lord Himself would be their eternal light. This is also prefigured by the Woman in the Apocalypse <note>The Book of Revelation 12:1.</note> who is clothed with the sun and has the moon under her feet.

The seven disciples who were gathered here as one, and who also boarded a ship together and worked together, signify the seven angels of the seven churches of **Jesus Christ**, of which one reads in Revelation <note>original: *Apoc.*, an abbreviation for the Apocalypse</note> chapters 1, 2, and 3. ### Answer.

Yes, I certainly find objection to it, and consider the word **Person** in the description of the holy **Godhead** <term>Godhead: The essential nature of God (German: *Gottheit*).</term> to be a completely improper and absurd expression; especially since in our **German way of speaking**, one indicates a specific human being through such a word. When one speaks of **three Persons** in the Godhead, or **three Divine Persons**, it implies—according to the literal meaning of the word—as if there were three distinct persons in the Godhead, separated from one another, just as if three human beings were together. This, however, is by no means the case; rather, there is only one **God** and a single, holy Being, who nevertheless reveals Himself in His outflowing in a **threefold property**. Therefore, I would certainly consider it more advisable if one were satisfied with the word of the **number three**, as John writes: *There are three that bear witness in heaven*, etc. <note>original: "Drey sind/ die da zeugen im Himmel / ꝛc." Referring to the 'Johannine Comma' in 1 John 5:7.</note>, and left out the word **Person**, because it is not to be found in **Holy Scripture** and was introduced by the ancients in a very thoughtless manner.

->Wherein one reveals his inner exercises of faith<-

that the more **GOD** reveals of His essence and perfection to even the most perfect creatures throughout all infinite eternity, the more unfathomable wonders, glories, and excellencies will still remain to be revealed in Him.

And this faith, it seems to me, places us above all deception; for what **God** is in Himself, that He is certainly and truly. It is impossible that this should not be true, or that he should be deceived who, with his understanding and will, grasps **God** in this general way, rather than modeling specific designs for himself through his own wit <note>In this 18th-century context, "wit" (Witz) refers to human cleverness or intellectual ingenuity rather than humor.</note>.

This faith is now, as it were, my element. In the entire visible and invisible world, there is only one Good and only one Evil: the former is the Will of **GOD**, the latter is the self-will <note>The German *Eigenwill* refers to the human ego's desire to act independently of God, a central theme in Pietist and mystical thought.</note> of the creature.

less to be feared in internal things than in external ones? In spiritual treasures than in physical ones? In the enjoyment of invisible things than in visible ones?

I mean, because self-will, self-pleasure, one’s own taste and delight took their beginning in the heavenly dwellings; and out of an angel full of heartiness <note>original: *Herzlichkeit*; in this context, it refers to the inner vitality or splendor of the angelic state before the fall</note>, it made a devil, overwhelmed with infinite misery; and out of a man made in the image of God, it made an image of the devil; it made a hell out of heaven, and a wretched abyss out of paradise.

So it is primarily in invisible and spiritual things that we must be strictly on guard against our own will—that we should fear it all the more, trust it all the less, and apply all the greater diligence to renounce it, to die to it, and to surrender ourselves entirely to the free and pleasing will of God, and to cling to Him so much more firmly in total and heartfelt denial of all self-pleasure, even in the most holy things. Thus, we should simply hand everything over to His alone-wise and alone-good providence <term>Schickung: God's sovereign arrangement or "sending" of circumstances</term>, so that He may act therein according to His good judgment and pleasure, and not according to ours:

Lest we perhaps, through a disordered attachment, ruin everything and turn into poison that which was given to us by God as medicine and strengthening for our weakness—namely, so that we might run all the more courageously upon the path of the Cross, of death, and of annihilation <term>Vernichtigung: a mystical term for the "naughting" of the self, where the individual ego is stripped away to make room for God</term>, from which, if we wish to be wise, we should not deviate by a single hair's breadth.

# The Sixth Letter.

## Also written by the author of the preceding letter.

->My dear brother!<-

Do not let it estrange you / that your sins now make you anxious and fearful / so that you must say: It is quite different with me / I am greatly crushed / and I howl from the great disquiet of my heart / etc. <note>The author is quoting Psalm 38:8: "I am feeble and sore broken: I have roared by reason of the disquietness of my heart."</note> For it must necessarily be so; and this is precisely the time / when God leads us to Hell <note>This refers to the "Law-work" or "terrors of the soul," a theological concept where a person must feel the weight of their own damnation before they can truly appreciate or receive God's grace.</note>; the time, however / when He leads us into Heaven / comes afterward / and when that time arrives / then mourning has an end.

Therefore / follow my counsel / and remain always inwardly within yourself during this time / in which the Lord visits you / and pay close attention to the concerns of your heart; and when you perceive / that it is so anxious and restless because of your sin / and that your thoughts accuse one another <note>A reference to Romans 2:15, describing the inner workings of the conscience.</note> / then do not deny it for long / but confess your sin to the Lord and ask Him for grace: for whoever denies his sin / will not succeed; but whoever confesses and forsakes them / shall obtain mercy. <note>A paraphrase of Proverbs 28:13.</note>

Seek also in your distress no comfort / nor help from men / for the help of men is of no use at such a time / but call upon God for help / so He will have mercy on you and help you. Fall at His feet in humility / and lament your need and misery to Him / and while doing so, consider yourself entirely unworthy of His grace and mercy; yet, despite this, rely upon His faithfulness,
